title: AI could end up too cheap to control
excerpt: In recent weeks, Chinese companies have released two AI models — Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max — that are nearly as powerful as ChatGPT and much less expensive.
content_html:
The AI industry’s investors and critics don’t agree on much. But many in each camp share at least one basic conviction: America’s top labs are about to make a killing.

Capital markets have signaled their faith in Anthropic and OpenAI’s impending hyper-profitability, valuing each at nearly $1 trillion. Many of Silicon Valley’s progressive adversaries also expect the labs to grow filthy rich but fear the implications, warning that AI-induced automation could transfer vast sums of money from ordinary workers to a handful of giant tech companies. Sen. Bernie Sanders’s call for nationalizing the top AI labs rests partly on that concern.

Key takeaways

  • The AI industry may be more competitive than investors expected.
  • Chinese labs are producing models nearly as powerful as Claude and ChatGPT — and dramatically cheaper.
  • That could make frontier AI a low-margin business.
  • A world of cheap, open-source AI would bring both promise and danger.

But recent advances in Chinese AI call all of this into question.

Over the past two months, Chinese companies have released three AI models that are nearly as powerful as America’s frontier systems — and radically less expensive.

In June, Beijing’s Z.ai debuted a model that performed nearly as well as Claude and ChatGPT’s second-tier systems on independent benchmarks. Weeks later, another Chinese firm, Moonshot, unveiled “Kimi K3,” a model that allegedly outperforms all of its American rivals except for the very latest versions of Claude and ChatGPT. Finally, just days ago, Alibaba launched a preview of Qwen3.8 Max, which purportedly outclasses even OpenAI’s most advanced systems, while trailing only Claude’s Fable in its capabilities. (Disclosure: Vox Media is one of several publishers that have signed partnership agreements with OpenAI. Our reporting remains editorially independent.)

These developments don’t merely threaten America’s AI giants with stiffer competition in the race for superintelligence. Rather, they raise a more harrowing prospect: that the AI race’s ultimate rewards will be far smaller than anticipated. In a world where new advances can regularly be leapfrogged by cheaper upstarts, hoarding the technology — and its profits — will be harder for any one company to do.

In other words, building a machine God might not be as lucrative as it’s cracked up to be. AI, it turns out, may “want to be free.”

How AI was supposed to pay off

To see how China’s new models threaten Anthropic’s profit expectations, we must first examine why those expectations have been so high.

This is not entirely self-evident. After all, AI labs aren’t much like the hyper-profitable tech giants of the 2010s. Facebook and Airbrb were relatively capital-light businesses with ultra-low marginal costs (adding a profile to Facebook or listing to Airbnb costs the companies virtually nothing). And once each gained a foothold in their respective markets, network effects enabled them to retain formidable positions without needing to constantly upgrade their products.

Building a state-of-the-art AI company is a much more involved — and astronomically more expensive — endeavor. To get to the frontier, Anthropic and OpenAI have sunk (at least) tens of billions into semiconductors, data centers, power plants, and other capital investments. Staying at the cutting-edge, meanwhile, compels them to perpetually churn out evermore costly models.

To put a new Claude model through its initial training — in which it spends months digesting the internet and sussing out statistical patterns within its text — can now cost hundreds of millions of dollars. And such foundational computation is only the beginning. A truly superlative model requires several additional months of fine-tuning. Armies of contracted experts — such as computer scientists, physicians, and mathematicians — tutor the models, grading their answers and guiding them towards better ones. Then the AI systems complete millions of rounds of practice, in which they learn through trial and error how to solve countless problems. This arduous process, known as “post-training,” compounds the costs of a single model’s development.

All of which raises the question: Why would investors expect businesses with a cost-structure this challenging to be not merely profitable, but massively so?

There are (at least) two answers. The first (and most obvious) is that the market for superintelligent machines is liable to be vast. Frontier AI systems promise to reduce costs and improve performance in myriad white-collar sectors. And Anthropic’s soaring revenues indicate that firms do, in fact, find Claude useful. A company like AirBnB has earned billions by revolutionizing a single industry; imagine then what a technology that remade virtually all industries might be worth.

Of course, plenty of technologies are valuable but not massively profitable to produce. After all, in well-functioning markets, competition should eventually erode individual firms’ margins, even if the underlying technology continues generating huge value.

But this is where the second answer comes in: Frontier labs’ immense costs are a burden, but they’re also a safeguard against competition — or, in industry parlance, a “moat.”

Startups may be able to afford to build or acquire more rudimentary models, many of which are “open source.” But, the thinking goes, they won’t be able to deliver Claude Fable-level performance without raising giant amounts of capital. And what investors will be willing to pour hundreds of billions into an AI pipsqueak that’s light-years behind Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI?

Alas, the Chinese AI labs’ rapid progress — and the way it was achieved — suggest that Anthropic’s moat may be shallower than previously thought.

How Moonshot swam Anthropic’s moat

The existence of powerful, Chinese AI systems is neither new nor surprising. Xi Jinping’s government has made vying for global AI dominance a key economic goal. And China’s DeepSeek, which also has stunned US companies with its lower-cost competitive models, surpassed ChatGPT as the most-downloaded free iPhone app more than a year ago.

The latest models, however, have dramatically narrowed the gap in capabilities between frontier American systems and their Chinese rivals. Just as critically, they’ve done so in a manner that other, relatively underfunded AI upstarts might be able to emulate.

Alibaba and Moonshot needed to invest massive resources to train their base models. But they allegedly found a low-cost way to refine those models into near-frontier systems: Just ask Claude.

Or, more specifically: Engage Claude in 16 million conversations, using 24,000 fake accounts. In each of those exchanges, ask the model to not only answer countless difficult questions but also, walk you through its reasoning, step by step. Then take all of this data and feed it into your own model as study material, training it to respond to the world’s most challenging queries as Claude would.

Through this process — known as “distillation” — an AI lab can replicate virtually all of a frontier model’s capacities, without sinking vast sums into human experts and post-training computing runs.

China’s AI labs have not admitted to using distillation. But OpenAI and Anthropic both reportedly uncovered Chinese distillation attempts earlier this year. And some of the new models appear to display tell-tale signs of distillation in conversations with ordinary users; Kimi K3 has routinely identified itself as “Claude.”

Chinese AI companies are hardly alone in using distillation to catch up with frontier labs. Earlier this year, Elon Musk admitted in court that xAI enhanced Grok’s capabilities by running distillation techniques on Claude and ChatGPT. Nonetheless, China’s latest models appear to demonstrate that distillation can help take a second-tier model to the frontier’s threshold.

America’s frontier labs have tried to defend themselves against such imitators. But this is technically difficult when distillers can assemble massive networks of bots, each asking an inconspicuous number of questions. And legally, it is difficult for America’s AI giants to argue that distillers are stealing their intellectual property. After all, in a sense, China’s copycats are merely doing to Anthropic and OpenAI what those companies did to journalists, coders, lawyers and other specialists: Feeding their public-facing outputs into a model, which then replicates their capabilities by discerning underlying patterns within the text.

Oh, and China’s giving these models away

The new Chinese models would have caused Silicon Valley enough headaches, if they merely provided stiffer competition, while demonstrating the power of distillation.

What makes Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max especially threatening to the American AI giants’ profitmaking potential, however, is that they are officially open source — meaning that the models’ parameters can be downloaded for free. (Alibaba and Moonshot have not yet released these parameters, but they say they will shortly.)

In other words, any company or hobbyist with enough computing power will soon be able to run a near-frontier Chinese model on their own hardware, modify that model to better serve a specialized purpose, and then sell access to their new version — without paying Alibiba a single yuan.

As Kimi and Qwen grow more capable, their market-share is likely to grow, at American AI giants’ expense.

For many of Anthropic and OpenAI’s potential customers, that proposition may be hard to turn down. Most businesses don’t need the world’s smartest AI, just one competent at their enterprise’s core tasks — compiling legal research, answering IT queries, writing working code, etc. A model that produces outputs 90 percent as good as Claude’s — at roughly one-sixth of the cost — will sound pretty good to many corporations.

Further, open source models aren’t just cheaper than frontier systems, but potentially more secure. If you run an AI on your firm’s own servers, then you don’t need to entrust sensitive data to Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI.

All this had led much of corporate America to embrace open-source models, even before the latest versions narrowed the capabilities gap. In a Linux Foundation survey, 63 percent of organizations reported using open-source AI systems.

And increasingly, those models are Chinese. According to Sequoia Capital, one of Silicon Valley’s premier venture capitalist firms, a majority of American AI startups now use open-source Chinese systems. As Kimi and Qwen grow more capable, their market-share is likely to grow, at American AI giants’ expense.

What’s bad for OpenAI is good (and/or catastrophic) for humanity

All this said, it is still entirely possible that OpenAI and Anthropic will justify their colossal valuations. In many highly competitive economic domains, having access to the world’s very best AI model will remain highly valuable. And America’s frontier labs still outperform all their peers.

But it’s increasingly plausible that selling state-of-the-art AI systems will prove to be a low-margin undertaking. In a world of ubiquitous, near-frontier open source models, the AI sector’s big winners probably won’t be its top labs, but rather, its chipmakers and cloud computing providers.

For ordinary people, a future where superintelligence is dirt cheap — and rival AI companies are constantly rising and falling, rather than consolidating into mega-corporations — would look somewhat different than the cyberpunk dystopia that the left’s been dreading.

And not entirely in a good way. For one thing, in that reality, mitigating AI’s biggest risks would be immensely difficult. Having a handful of firms monopolize control over frontier AI systems is bad in many respects. But it does make those models easier to regulate, as the Trump administration’s decision to temporarily block Claude’s Fable in the name of cybersecurity demonstrated.

By contrast, if recipes for ultra-powerful AI models are published all over the internet — and anyone with modest technical skills can modify them at will — then systems willing to help their users hack government bureaucracies or engineer bio-weapons are liable to proliferate.

From another angle, however, the “AI becomes almost free” scenario may look like capitalism at its finest: Retrospectively, such a development would mean that a small number of extremely rich people bankrolled the creation of an immensely useful technology, under the expectation of massive profits, only to see competition erode their returns — and disperse that tech’s benefits across a wider group of businesses and consumers.

Granted, in the case of AI, this process might also generate a super-virus that kills us all. But hey, no system is perfect.

sentences.en: How AI was supposed to pay off
sentences.zh: 人工智能应该如何获得回报

blocks.html_en: To see how China’s new models threaten Anthropic’s profit expectations, we must first examine why those expectations have been so high.

sentences.en: To see how China’s new models threaten Anthropic’s profit expectations, we must first examine why those expectations have been so high.
sentences.zh: 要了解中国的新模式如何威胁 Anthropic 的利润预期，我们必须首先研究为什么这些预期如此之高。

blocks.html_en: This is not entirely self-evident. After all, AI labs aren’t much like the hyper-profitable tech giants of the 2010s. Facebook and Airbrb were relatively capital-light businesses with ultra-low marginal costs (adding a profile to Facebook or listing to Airbnb costs the companies virtually nothing). And once each gained a foothold in their respective markets, network effects enabled them to retain formidable positions without needing to constantly upgrade their products.

sentences.en: This is not entirely self-evident.
sentences.zh: 这并不完全是不言而喻的。

sentences.en: After all, AI labs aren’t much like the hyper-profitable tech giants of the 2010s.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，人工智能实验室与 2010 年代利润丰厚的科技巨头不太一样。

sentences.en: Facebook and Airbrb were relatively capital-light businesses with ultra-low marginal costs (adding a profile to Facebook or listing to Airbnb costs the companies virtually nothing).
sentences.zh: Facebook 和 Airbrb 是资本相对较少的企业，边际成本极低（在 Facebook 上添加个人资料或在 Airbnb 上列出信息，公司几乎不需要任何成本）。

sentences.en: And once each gained a foothold in their respective markets, network effects enabled them to retain formidable positions without needing to constantly upgrade their products.
sentences.zh: 一旦每个公司在各自的市场站稳脚跟，网络效应就使他们能够保持强大的地位，而无需不断升级产品。

blocks.html_en: Building a state-of-the-art AI company is a much more involved — and astronomically more expensive — endeavor. To get to the frontier, Anthropic and OpenAI have sunk (at least) tens of billions into semiconductors, data centers, power plants, and other capital investments. Staying at the cutting-edge, meanwhile, compels them to perpetually churn out evermore costly models.

sentences.en: Building a state-of-the-art AI company is a much more involved — and astronomically more expensive — endeavor.
sentences.zh: 建立一家最先进的人工智能公司是一项更加复杂的工作，而且成本也更高。

sentences.en: To get to the frontier, Anthropic and OpenAI have sunk (at least) tens of billions into semiconductors, data centers, power plants, and other capital investments.
sentences.zh: 为了达到这一前沿，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 已经在半导体、数据中心、发电厂和其他资本投资中投入了（至少）数百亿美元。

sentences.en: Staying at the cutting-edge, meanwhile, compels them to perpetually churn out evermore costly models.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，保持领先地位迫使他们不断地生产出越来越昂贵的型号。

blocks.html_en: To put a new Claude model through its initial training — in which it spends months digesting the internet and sussing out statistical patterns within its text — can now cost hundreds of millions of dollars. And such foundational computation is only the beginning. A truly superlative model requires several additional months of fine-tuning. Armies of contracted experts — such as computer scientists, physicians, and mathematicians — tutor the models, grading their answers and guiding them towards better ones. Then the AI systems complete millions of rounds of practice, in which they learn through trial and error how to solve countless problems. This arduous process, known as “post-training,” compounds the costs of a single model’s development.

sentences.en: To put a new Claude model through its initial training — in which it spends months digesting the internet and sussing out statistical patterns within its text — can now cost hundreds of millions of dollars.
sentences.zh: 要让一个新的克劳德模型通过初始训练——它需要花费数月时间消化互联网并找出文本中的统计模式——现在可能需要花费数亿美元。

sentences.en: And such foundational computation is only the beginning.
sentences.zh: 这种基础计算仅仅是开始。

sentences.en: A truly superlative model requires several additional months of fine-tuning.
sentences.zh: 真正最高级的模型需要额外几个月的微调。

sentences.en: Armies of contracted experts — such as computer scientists, physicians, and mathematicians — tutor the models, grading their answers and guiding them towards better ones.
sentences.zh: 大批签约专家——例如计算机科学家、医生和数学家——对模型进行指导，对他们的答案进行评分，并指导他们找到更好的答案。

sentences.en: Then the AI systems complete millions of rounds of practice, in which they learn through trial and error how to solve countless problems.
sentences.zh: 然后，人工智能系统完成数百万轮练习，通过反复试验学习如何解决无数问题。

sentences.en: This arduous process, known as “post-training,” compounds the costs of a single model’s development.
sentences.zh: 这个艰巨的过程被称为“训练后”，增加了单个模型的开发成本。

blocks.html_en: All of which raises the question: Why would investors expect businesses with a cost-structure this challenging to be not merely profitable, but massively so?

sentences.en: All of which raises the question: Why would investors expect businesses with a cost-structure this challenging to be not merely profitable, but massively so?
sentences.zh: 所有这些都提出了一个问题：为什么投资者期望成本结构如此具有挑战性的企业不仅能够盈利，而且能够大幅盈利？

blocks.html_en: There are (at least) two answers. The first (and most obvious) is that the market for superintelligent machines is liable to be vast. Frontier AI systems promise to reduce costs and improve performance in myriad white-collar sectors. And Anthropic’s soaring revenues indicate that firms do, in fact, find Claude useful. A company like AirBnB has earned billions by revolutionizing a single industry; imagine then what a technology that remade virtually all industries might be worth.

sentences.en: There are (at least) two answers.
sentences.zh: （至少）有两个答案。

sentences.en: The first (and most obvious) is that the market for superintelligent machines is liable to be vast.
sentences.zh: 第一个（也是最明显的）是超级智能机器的市场可能是巨大的。

sentences.en: Frontier AI systems promise to reduce costs and improve performance in myriad white-collar sectors.
sentences.zh: 前沿人工智能系统有望降低众多白领行业的成本并提高绩效。

sentences.en: And Anthropic’s soaring revenues indicate that firms do, in fact, find Claude useful.
sentences.zh: Anthropic 不断飙升的收入表明，公司实际上确实发现了克劳德的用处。

sentences.en: A company like AirBnB has earned billions by revolutionizing a single industry; imagine then what a technology that remade virtually all industries might be worth.
sentences.zh: 像爱彼迎这样的公司通过彻底改变单一行业赚取了数十亿美元的收入；那么想象一下，一项几乎重塑所有行业的技术可能值多少钱。

blocks.html_en: Of course, plenty of technologies are valuable but not massively profitable to produce. After all, in well-functioning markets, competition should eventually erode individual firms’ margins, even if the underlying technology continues generating huge value.

sentences.en: Of course, plenty of technologies are valuable but not massively profitable to produce.
sentences.zh: 当然，许多技术很有价值，但生产起来利润并不高。

sentences.en: After all, in well-functioning markets, competition should eventually erode individual firms’ margins, even if the underlying technology continues generating huge value.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，在运作良好的市场中，即使基础技术继续创造巨大价值，竞争最终也会侵蚀个别公司的利润。

blocks.html_en: But this is where the second answer comes in: Frontier labs’ immense costs are a burden, but they’re also a safeguard against competition — or, in industry parlance, a “moat.”

sentences.en: But this is where the second answer comes in: Frontier labs’ immense costs are a burden, but they’re also a safeguard against competition — or, in industry parlance, a “moat.”
sentences.zh: 但这就是第二个答案的来源：前沿实验室的巨大成本是一种负担，但它们也是对抗竞争的保障——或者用行业术语来说，是一条“护城河”。

blocks.html_en: Startups may be able to afford to build or acquire more rudimentary models, many of which are “open source.” But, the thinking goes, they won’t be able to deliver Claude Fable-level performance without raising giant amounts of capital. And what investors will be willing to pour hundreds of billions into an AI pipsqueak that’s light-years behind Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI?

sentences.en: Startups may be able to afford to build or acquire more rudimentary models, many of which are “open source.”
sentences.zh: 初创公司可能有能力构建或获取更基本的模型，其中许多是“开源的”。

sentences.en: But, the thinking goes, they won’t be able to deliver Claude Fable-level performance without raising giant amounts of capital.
sentences.zh: 但是，人们的想法是，如果不筹集大量资金，他们将无法实现克劳德·寓言级别的业绩。

sentences.en: And what investors will be willing to pour hundreds of billions into an AI pipsqueak that’s light-years behind Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI?
sentences.zh: 哪些投资者会愿意向这家落后谷歌、Anthropic 和 OpenAI 几光年的人工智能公司投入数千亿美元？

blocks.html_en: Alas, the Chinese AI labs’ rapid progress — and the way it was achieved — suggest that Anthropic’s moat may be shallower than previously thought.

sentences.en: Alas, the Chinese AI labs’ rapid progress — and the way it was achieved — suggest that Anthropic’s moat may be shallower than previously thought.
sentences.zh: 可惜的是，中国人工智能实验室的快速进步及其实现方式表明，Anthropic 的护城河可能比之前想象的要浅。

blocks.html_en: How Moonshot swam Anthropic’s moat

sentences.en: How Moonshot swam Anthropic’s moat
sentences.zh: Moonshot 如何跨越 Anthropic 的护城河

blocks.html_en: The existence of powerful, Chinese AI systems is neither new nor surprising. Xi Jinping’s government has made vying for global AI dominance a key economic goal. And China’s DeepSeek, which also has stunned US companies with its lower-cost competitive models, surpassed ChatGPT as the most-downloaded free iPhone app more than a year ago.

sentences.en: The existence of powerful, Chinese AI systems is neither new nor surprising.
sentences.zh: 强大的中国人工智能系统的存在既不新鲜也不令人惊讶。

sentences.en: Xi Jinping’s government has made vying for global AI dominance a key economic goal.
sentences.zh: 习近平政府已将争夺全球人工智能主导地位作为一项关键的经济目标。

sentences.en: And China’s DeepSeek, which also has stunned US companies with its lower-cost competitive models, surpassed ChatGPT as the most-downloaded free iPhone app more than a year ago.
sentences.zh: 中国的 DeepSeek 也以其低成本的竞争模式震惊了美国公司，一年多前就超越 ChatGPT 成为下载次数最多的免费 iPhone 应用程序。

blocks.html_en: The latest models, however, have dramatically narrowed the gap in capabilities between frontier American systems and their Chinese rivals. Just as critically, they’ve done so in a manner that other, relatively underfunded AI upstarts might be able to emulate.

sentences.en: The latest models, however, have dramatically narrowed the gap in capabilities between frontier American systems and their Chinese rivals.
sentences.zh: 然而，最新型号极大地缩小了美国前沿系统与其中国竞争对手之间的能力差距。

sentences.en: Just as critically, they’ve done so in a manner that other, relatively underfunded AI upstarts might be able to emulate.
sentences.zh: 同样重要的是，他们这样做的方式可能是其他资金相对不足的人工智能新贵可以效仿的。

blocks.html_en: Alibaba and Moonshot needed to invest massive resources to train their base models. But they allegedly found a low-cost way to refine those models into near-frontier systems: Just ask Claude.

sentences.en: Alibaba and Moonshot needed to invest massive resources to train their base models.
sentences.zh: 阿里巴巴和 Moonshot 需要投入大量资源来训练他们的基础模型。

sentences.en: But they allegedly found a low-cost way to refine those models into near-frontier systems: Just ask Claude.
sentences.zh: 但据称他们找到了一种低成本方法将这些模型改进为近前沿系统：只要问克劳德即可。

blocks.html_en: Or, more specifically: Engage Claude in 16 million conversations, using 24,000 fake accounts. In each of those exchanges, ask the model to not only answer countless difficult questions but also, walk you through its reasoning, step by step. Then take all of this data and feed it into your own model as study material, training it to respond to the world’s most challenging queries as Claude would.

sentences.en: Or, more specifically: Engage Claude in 16 million conversations, using 24,000 fake accounts.
sentences.zh: 或者，更具体地说：使用 24,000 个虚假帐户与 Claude 进行 1,600 万次对话。

sentences.en: In each of those exchanges, ask the model to not only answer countless difficult questions but also, walk you through its reasoning, step by step.
sentences.zh: 在每次交流中，要求模型不仅回答无数难题，而且一步步引导您完成其推理。

sentences.en: Then take all of this data and feed it into your own model as study material, training it to respond to the world’s most challenging queries as Claude would.
sentences.zh: 然后将所有这些数据作为学习材料输入到您自己的模型中，训练它像 Claude 一样响应世界上最具挑战性的查询。

blocks.html_en: Through this process — known as “distillation” — an AI lab can replicate virtually all of a frontier model’s capacities, without sinking vast sums into human experts and post-training computing runs.

sentences.en: Through this process — known as “distillation” — an AI lab can replicate virtually all of a frontier model’s capacities, without sinking vast sums into human experts and post-training computing runs.
sentences.zh: 通过这个被称为“蒸馏”的过程，人工智能实验室可以复制几乎所有前沿模型的功能，而无需在人类专家和训练后计算运行中投入大量资金。

blocks.html_en: China’s AI labs have not admitted to using distillation. But OpenAI and Anthropic both reportedly uncovered Chinese distillation attempts earlier this year. And some of the new models appear to display tell-tale signs of distillation in conversations with ordinary users; Kimi K3 has routinely identified itself as “Claude.”

sentences.en: China’s AI labs have not admitted to using distillation.
sentences.zh: 中国的人工智能实验室尚未承认使用蒸馏法。

sentences.en: But OpenAI and Anthropic both reportedly uncovered Chinese distillation attempts earlier this year.
sentences.zh: 但据报道，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 今年早些时候都发现了中国的蒸馏尝试。

sentences.en: And some of the new models appear to display tell-tale signs of distillation in conversations with ordinary users; Kimi K3 has routinely identified itself as “Claude.”
sentences.zh: 一些新型号似乎在与普通用户的对话中显示出明显的蒸馏迹象。 Kimi K3 通常将自己称为“克劳德”。

blocks.html_en: Chinese AI companies are hardly alone in using distillation to catch up with frontier labs. Earlier this year, Elon Musk admitted in court that xAI enhanced Grok’s capabilities by running distillation techniques on Claude and ChatGPT. Nonetheless, China’s latest models appear to demonstrate that distillation can help take a second-tier model to the frontier’s threshold.

sentences.en: Chinese AI companies are hardly alone in using distillation to catch up with frontier labs.
sentences.zh: 中国的人工智能公司并不是唯一一家利用蒸馏技术赶超前沿实验室的公司。

sentences.en: Earlier this year, Elon Musk admitted in court that xAI enhanced Grok’s capabilities by running distillation techniques on Claude and ChatGPT.
sentences.zh: 今年早些时候，埃隆·马斯克在法庭上承认，xAI 通过在 Claude 和 ChatGPT 上运行蒸馏技术增强了 Grok 的功能。

sentences.en: Nonetheless, China’s latest models appear to demonstrate that distillation can help take a second-tier model to the frontier’s threshold.
sentences.zh: 尽管如此，中国的最新模型似乎表明，蒸馏可以帮助将二线模型推向前沿。

blocks.html_en: America’s frontier labs have tried to defend themselves against such imitators. But this is technically difficult when distillers can assemble massive networks of bots, each asking an inconspicuous number of questions. And legally, it is difficult for America’s AI giants to argue that distillers are stealing their intellectual property. After all, in a sense, China’s copycats are merely doing to Anthropic and OpenAI what those companies did to journalists, coders, lawyers and other specialists: Feeding their public-facing outputs into a model, which then replicates their capabilities by discerning underlying patterns within the text.

sentences.en: America’s frontier labs have tried to defend themselves against such imitators.
sentences.zh: 美国的前沿实验室试图抵御此类模仿者。

sentences.en: But this is technically difficult when distillers can assemble massive networks of bots, each asking an inconspicuous number of questions.
sentences.zh: 但当蒸馏器可以组装庞大的机器人网络时，这在技术上是困难的，每个机器人都会提出一些不起眼的问题。

sentences.en: And legally, it is difficult for America’s AI giants to argue that distillers are stealing their intellectual property.
sentences.zh: 从法律上讲，美国的人工智能巨头很难辩称酿酒厂正在窃取他们的知识产权。

sentences.en: After all, in a sense, China’s copycats are merely doing to Anthropic and OpenAI what those companies did to journalists, coders, lawyers and other specialists: Feeding their public-facing outputs into a model, which then replicates their capabilities by discerning underlying patterns within the text.
sentences.zh: 毕竟，从某种意义上说，中国的模仿者只是对 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 做了这些公司对记者、程序员、律师和其他专家所做的事情：将他们面向公众的输出输入到模型中，然后模型通过识别文本中的潜在模式来复制他们的能力。

blocks.html_en: Oh, and China’s giving these models away

sentences.en: Oh, and China’s giving these models away
sentences.zh: 哦，中国正在赠送这些模型

blocks.html_en: The new Chinese models would have caused Silicon Valley enough headaches, if they merely provided stiffer competition, while demonstrating the power of distillation.

sentences.en: The new Chinese models would have caused Silicon Valley enough headaches, if they merely provided stiffer competition, while demonstrating the power of distillation.
sentences.zh: 如果新的中国模式仅仅提供更激烈的竞争，同时展示蒸馏的力量，它们就会给硅谷带来足够多的麻烦。

blocks.html_en: What makes Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max especially threatening to the American AI giants’ profitmaking potential, however, is that they are officially open source — meaning that the models’ parameters can be downloaded for free. (Alibaba and Moonshot have not yet released these parameters, but they say they will shortly.)

sentences.en: What makes Kimi K3 and Qwen3.8 Max especially threatening to the American AI giants’ profitmaking potential, however, is that they are officially open source — meaning that the models’ parameters can be downloaded for free.
sentences.zh: 然而，Kimi K3 和 Qwen3.8 Max 对美国人工智能巨头的盈利潜力尤其构成威胁，因为它们是正式开源的，这意味着模型的参数可以免费下载。

sentences.en: (Alibaba and Moonshot have not yet released these parameters, but they say they will shortly.)
sentences.zh: （阿里巴巴和 Moonshot 尚未发布这些参数，但他们表示很快就会发布。）

blocks.html_en: In other words, any company or hobbyist with enough computing power will soon be able to run a near-frontier Chinese model on their own hardware, modify that model to better serve a specialized purpose, and then sell access to their new version — without paying Alibiba a single yuan.

sentences.en: In other words, any company or hobbyist with enough computing power will soon be able to run a near-frontier Chinese model on their own hardware, modify that model to better serve a specialized purpose, and then sell access to their new version — without paying Alibiba a single yuan.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，任何拥有足够计算能力的公司或爱好者很快就能够在自己的硬件上运行近乎前沿的中国模型，修改该模型以更好地服务于特定目的，然后出售其新版本的访问权，而无需向阿里巴巴支付一分钱。

blocks.html_en: As Kimi and Qwen grow more capable, their market-share is likely to grow, at American AI giants’ expense.

sentences.en: As Kimi and Qwen grow more capable, their market-share is likely to grow, at American AI giants’ expense.
sentences.zh: 随着 Kimi 和 Qwen 的能力不断增强，他们的市场份额可能会增加，但美国人工智能巨头的份额可能会受到损害。

blocks.html_en: For many of Anthropic and OpenAI’s potential customers, that proposition may be hard to turn down. Most businesses don’t need the world’s smartest AI, just one competent at their enterprise’s core tasks — compiling legal research, answering IT queries, writing working code, etc. A model that produces outputs 90 percent as good as Claude’s — at roughly one-sixth of the cost — will sound pretty good to many corporations.

sentences.en: For many of Anthropic and OpenAI’s potential customers, that proposition may be hard to turn down.
sentences.zh: 对于 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的许多潜在客户来说，这个提议可能很难拒绝。

sentences.en: Most businesses don’t need the world’s smartest AI, just one competent at their enterprise’s core tasks — compiling legal research, answering IT queries, writing working code, etc. A model that produces outputs 90 percent as good as Claude’s — at roughly one-sixth of the cost — will sound pretty good to many corporations.
sentences.zh: 大多数企业不需要世界上最聪明的人工智能，只需要一个能够胜任企业核心任务的人工智能——编译法律研究、回答 IT 查询、编写工作代码等。对于许多公司来说，一个产出与 Claude 的 90% 一样好的模型——成本大约是六分之一——听起来相当不错。

blocks.html_en: Further, open source models aren’t just cheaper than frontier systems, but potentially more secure. If you run an AI on your firm’s own servers, then you don’t need to entrust sensitive data to Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI.

sentences.en: Further, open source models aren’t just cheaper than frontier systems, but potentially more secure.
sentences.zh: 此外，开源模型不仅比前沿系统便宜，而且可能更安全。

sentences.en: If you run an AI on your firm’s own servers, then you don’t need to entrust sensitive data to Anthropic, Google, or OpenAI.
sentences.zh: 如果您在公司自己的服务器上运行人工智能，那么您不需要将敏感数据委托给 Anthropic、Google 或 OpenAI。

blocks.html_en: All this had led much of corporate America to embrace open-source models, even before the latest versions narrowed the capabilities gap. In a Linux Foundation survey, 63 percent of organizations reported using open-source AI systems.

sentences.en: All this had led much of corporate America to embrace open-source models, even before the latest versions narrowed the capabilities gap.
sentences.zh: 所有这些都导致美国许多企业接受开源模型，甚至在最新版本缩小能力差距之前也是如此。

sentences.en: In a Linux Foundation survey, 63 percent of organizations reported using open-source AI systems.
sentences.zh: 在 Linux 基金会的一项调查中，63% 的组织报告使用开源人工智能系统。

blocks.html_en: And increasingly, those models are Chinese. According to Sequoia Capital, one of Silicon Valley’s premier venture capitalist firms, a majority of American AI startups now use open-source Chinese systems. As Kimi and Qwen grow more capable, their market-share is likely to grow, at American AI giants’ expense.

sentences.en: And increasingly, those models are Chinese.
sentences.zh: 而且这些模特越来越多地是中国人。

sentences.en: According to Sequoia Capital, one of Silicon Valley’s premier venture capitalist firms, a majority of American AI startups now use open-source Chinese systems.
sentences.zh: 据硅谷主要风险投资公司之一红杉资本称，大多数美国人工智能初创公司现在都使用开源的中国系统。

sentences.en: As Kimi and Qwen grow more capable, their market-share is likely to grow, at American AI giants’ expense.
sentences.zh: 随着 Kimi 和 Qwen 的能力不断增强，他们的市场份额可能会增加，但美国人工智能巨头的份额可能会受到损害。

blocks.html_en: What’s bad for OpenAI is good (and/or catastrophic) for humanity

sentences.en: What’s bad for OpenAI is good (and/or catastrophic) for humanity
sentences.zh: 对 OpenAI 不利的事情对人类来说却是好事（和/或灾难性的）

blocks.html_en: All this said, it is still entirely possible that OpenAI and Anthropic will justify their colossal valuations. content_html_zh:
人工智能行业的投资者和批评者的看法并不一致。 但每个阵营中的许多人都至少有一个基本信念：美国的顶级实验室即将大赚一笔。

资本市场已经表明了他们对 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 即将实现的超额盈利能力的信心，两家公司的估值均接近 1 万亿美元。 硅谷的许多进步对手也预计实验室会变得非常富有，但担心其影响，警告人工智能引发的自动化可能会将大量资金从普通工人转移到少数大型科技公司。 它是。 伯尼·桑德斯 (Bernie Sanders) 呼吁将顶级人工智能实验室国有化，部分原因在于这种担忧。

要点

  • 人工智能行业的竞争可能比投资者预期的更加激烈。
  • 中国实验室正在生产几乎与 Claude 和 ChatGPT 一样强大的模型，而且价格便宜得多。
  • 这可能会使前沿人工智能成为低利润业务。
  • 廉价、开源人工智能的世界既带来希望，也带来危险。

但中国人工智能的最新进展让这一切都受到质疑。

在过去的两个月里，中国公司发布了三种人工智能模型，它们的功能几乎与美国的前沿系统一样强大，而且价格便宜得多。

6 月，北京的 Z.ai 推出了一个模型，该模型在独立基准测试中的表现几乎与 Claude 和 ChatGPT 的第二层系统一样好。 几周后，另一家中国公司 Moonshot 推出了“Kimi K3”，据称该型号的性能优于除最新版本的 Claude 和 ChatGPT 之外的所有美国竞争对手。 最后，就在几天前，阿里巴巴推出了 Qwen3.8 Max 的预览版，据称它甚至超越了 OpenAI 最先进的系统，而其功能仅落后于 Claude’s Fable。 （披露：Vox Media 是与 OpenAI 签署合作伙伴协议的几家出版商之一。 我们的报道保持编辑独立性。）

这些发展不仅对美国人工智能巨头构成超级智能竞赛中更激烈的竞争的威胁。 相反，他们提出了一个更令人痛苦的前景：人工智能竞赛的最终回报将远远小于预期。 在一个新的进步经常会被更便宜的新贵超越的世界里，囤积技术及其利润对于任何一家公司来说都将变得更加困难。

换句话说，建造一个机器神可能并不像人们吹捧的那样有利可图。 事实证明，人工智能可能“想要自由”。

人工智能应该如何获得回报

要了解中国的新模式如何威胁 Anthropic 的利润预期，我们必须首先研究为什么这些预期如此之高。

这并不完全是不言而喻的。 毕竟，人工智能实验室与 2010 年代利润丰厚的科技巨头不太一样。 Facebook 和 Airbrb 是资本相对较少的企业，边际成本极低（在 Facebook 上添加个人资料或在 Airbnb 上列出信息，公司几乎不需要任何成本）。 一旦每个公司在各自的市场站稳脚跟，网络效应就使他们能够保持强大的地位，而无需不断升级产品。

建立一家最先进的人工智能公司是一项更加复杂的工作，而且成本也更高。 为了达到这一前沿，Anthropic 和 OpenAI 已经在半导体、数据中心、发电厂和其他资本投资中投入了（至少）数百亿美元。 与此同时，保持领先地位迫使他们不断地生产出越来越昂贵的型号。

要让一个新的克劳德模型通过初始训练——它需要花费数月时间消化互联网并找出文本中的统计模式——现在可能需要花费数亿美元。 这种基础计算仅仅是开始。 真正最高级的模型需要额外几个月的微调。 大批签约专家——例如计算机科学家、医生和数学家——对模型进行指导，对他们的答案进行评分，并指导他们找到更好的答案。 然后，人工智能系统完成数百万轮练习，通过反复试验学习如何解决无数问题。 这个艰巨的过程被称为“训练后”，增加了单个模型的开发成本。

所有这些都提出了一个问题：为什么投资者期望成本结构如此具有挑战性的企业不仅能够盈利，而且能够大幅盈利？

（至少）有两个答案。 第一个（也是最明显的）是超级智能机器的市场可能是巨大的。 前沿人工智能系统有望降低众多白领行业的成本并提高绩效。 Anthropic 不断飙升的收入表明，公司实际上确实发现了克劳德的用处。 像爱彼迎这样的公司通过彻底改变单一行业赚取了数十亿美元的收入；那么想象一下，一项几乎重塑所有行业的技术可能值多少钱。

当然，许多技术很有价值，但生产起来利润并不高。 毕竟，在运作良好的市场中，即使基础技术继续创造巨大价值，竞争最终也会侵蚀个别公司的利润。

但这就是第二个答案的来源：前沿实验室的巨大成本是一种负担，但它们也是对抗竞争的保障——或者用行业术语来说，是一条“护城河”。

初创公司可能有能力构建或获取更基本的模型，其中许多是“开源的”。 但是，人们的想法是，如果不筹集大量资金，他们将无法实现克劳德·寓言级别的业绩。 哪些投资者会愿意向这家落后谷歌、Anthropic 和 OpenAI 几光年的人工智能公司投入数千亿美元？

可惜的是，中国人工智能实验室的快速进步及其实现方式表明，Anthropic 的护城河可能比之前想象的要浅。

Moonshot 如何跨越 Anthropic 的护城河

强大的中国人工智能系统的存在既不新鲜也不令人惊讶。 习近平政府已将争夺全球人工智能主导地位作为一项关键的经济目标。 中国的 DeepSeek 也以其低成本的竞争模式震惊了美国公司，一年多前就超越 ChatGPT 成为下载次数最多的免费 iPhone 应用程序。

然而，最新型号极大地缩小了美国前沿系统与其中国竞争对手之间的能力差距。 同样重要的是，他们这样做的方式可能是其他资金相对不足的人工智能新贵可以效仿的。

阿里巴巴和 Moonshot 需要投入大量资源来训练他们的基础模型。 但据称他们找到了一种低成本方法将这些模型改进为近前沿系统：只要问克劳德即可。

或者，更具体地说：使用 24,000 个虚假帐户与 Claude 进行 1,600 万次对话。 在每次交流中，要求模型不仅回答无数难题，而且一步步引导您完成其推理。 然后将所有这些数据作为学习材料输入到您自己的模型中，训练它像 Claude 一样响应世界上最具挑战性的查询。

通过这个被称为“蒸馏”的过程，人工智能实验室可以复制几乎所有前沿模型的功能，而无需在人类专家和训练后计算运行中投入大量资金。

中国的人工智能实验室尚未承认使用蒸馏法。 但据报道，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 今年早些时候都发现了中国的蒸馏尝试。 一些新型号似乎在与普通用户的对话中显示出明显的蒸馏迹象。 Kimi K3 通常将自己称为“克劳德”。

中国的人工智能公司并不是唯一一家利用蒸馏技术赶超前沿实验室的公司。 今年早些时候，埃隆·马斯克在法庭上承认，xAI 通过在 Claude 和 ChatGPT 上运行蒸馏技术增强了 Grok 的功能。 尽管如此，中国的最新模型似乎表明，蒸馏可以帮助将二线模型推向前沿。

美国的前沿实验室试图抵御此类模仿者。 但当蒸馏器可以组装庞大的机器人网络时，这在技术上是困难的，每个机器人都会提出一些不起眼的问题。 从法律上讲，美国的人工智能巨头很难辩称酿酒厂正在窃取他们的知识产权。 毕竟，从某种意义上说，中国的模仿者只是对 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 做了这些公司对记者、程序员、律师和其他专家所做的事情：将他们面向公众的输出输入到模型中，然后模型通过识别文本中的潜在模式来复制他们的能力。

哦，中国正在赠送这些模型

如果新的中国模式仅仅提供更激烈的竞争，同时展示蒸馏的力量，它们就会给硅谷带来足够多的麻烦。

然而，Kimi K3 和 Qwen3.8 Max 对美国人工智能巨头的盈利潜力尤其构成威胁，因为它们是正式开源的，这意味着模型的参数可以免费下载。 （阿里巴巴和 Moonshot 尚未发布这些参数，但他们表示很快就会发布。）

换句话说，任何拥有足够计算能力的公司或爱好者很快就能够在自己的硬件上运行近乎前沿的中国模型，修改该模型以更好地服务于特定目的，然后出售其新版本的访问权，而无需向阿里巴巴支付一分钱。

随着 Kimi 和 Qwen 的能力不断增强，他们的市场份额可能会增加，但美国人工智能巨头的份额可能会受到损害。

对于 Anthropic 和 OpenAI 的许多潜在客户来说，这个提议可能很难拒绝。 大多数企业不需要世界上最聪明的人工智能，只需要一个能够胜任企业核心任务的人工智能——编译法律研究、回答 IT 查询、编写工作代码等。对于许多公司来说，一个产出与 Claude 的 90% 一样好的模型——成本大约是六分之一——听起来相当不错。

此外，开源模型不仅比前沿系统便宜，而且可能更安全。 如果您在公司自己的服务器上运行人工智能，那么您不需要将敏感数据委托给 Anthropic、Google 或 OpenAI。

所有这些都导致美国许多企业接受开源模型，甚至在最新版本缩小能力差距之前也是如此。 在 Linux 基金会的一项调查中，63% 的组织报告使用开源人工智能系统。

而且这些模特越来越多地是中国人。 据硅谷主要风险投资公司之一红杉资本称，大多数美国人工智能初创公司现在都使用开源的中国系统。 随着 Kimi 和 Qwen 的能力不断增强，他们的市场份额可能会增加，但美国人工智能巨头的份额可能会受到损害。

对 OpenAI 不利的事情对人类来说却是好事（和/或灾难性的）

尽管如此，OpenAI 和 Anthropic 仍然完全有可能证明其巨大估值是合理的。 在许多竞争激烈的经济领域，获得世界上最好的人工智能模型仍然非常有价值。 美国的前沿实验室仍然优于所有同行。

但越来越有可能的是，销售最先进的人工智能系统将被证明是一项低利润的事业。 在一个无处不在、近乎前沿的开源模型的世界中，人工智能领域的大赢家可能不会是其顶级实验室，而是其芯片制造商和云计算提供商。

对于普通人来说，未来的超级智能非常便宜——而竞争对手的人工智能公司不断兴衰，而不是整合成巨型企业——看起来与左派一直害怕的赛博朋克反乌托邦有些不同。

而且并不完全是以一种好的方式。 一方面，在现实中，减轻人工智能最大的风险将是非常困难的。 让少数公司垄断前沿人工智能系统的控制权在很多方面都是糟糕的。 但它确实使这些模型更容易监管，特朗普政府决定以网络安全的名义暂时阻止克劳德的寓言就证明了这一点。

相比之下，如果超强大人工智能模型的配方在整个互联网上发布——任何具有适度技术技能的人都可以随意修改它们——那么愿意帮助用户破解政府官僚机构或设计生物武器的系统很可能会激增。

然而，从另一个角度来看，“人工智能变得几乎免费”的场景可能看起来像最好的资本主义：回顾过去，这种发展意味着少数极其富有的人在巨额利润的预期下资助创造一种极其有用的技术，结果却看到竞争侵蚀了他们的回报，并将技术的好处分散到更广泛的企业和消费者群体中。

诚然，就人工智能而言，这个过程也可能会产生一种杀死我们所有人的超级病毒。 但是，嘿，没有一个系统是完美的。
